**My reasoning:**

I farm about 10 mu of contracted land outside the village, same plot my family has worked for years. The soil is medium-loamy — decent for grains but needs water because rainfall here is never enough. Like every household around me, I grow winter wheat then summer maize on the same ground. That rotation is what I know, what the buyers expect, and what the input suppliers stock for. I don't have the capital or irrigation equipment to shift to vegetables or cotton, and frankly the risk isn't worth it at my age with kids still in school.

For the wheat I'll use a county-recommended improved variety — probably Jimai 22 or whatever the township extension office pushed last season. I won't try experimental seed; I need reliable germination. I'll apply base fertilizer before rotary tilling, then topdress urea at jointing. I'll irrigate three times: winter water before freeze, jointing water, and heading water. That's standard here and my neighbors all do the same.

After wheat harvest in June I'll direct-seed the maize into the stubble — no time for deep tillage. Hybrid seed is the only option anyone uses anymore; I buy郑单958 or a similar mid-maturity hybrid. Maize mostly rides the summer rains but I'll pump once if July is dry. One herbicide pass early on, one insecticide spray for corn borer mid-season.

I'm not going to push yields beyond what this land consistently delivers. I expect around 460 kg/mu on wheat and 560 on maize. That covers the household grain needs and leaves enough to sell.
